title: Rubber tyred gantry crane
wikitext:
{{Short description|Mobile crane used in intermodal operations to ground or stack containers}}
[[File:Intermodal terminal loading.jpg|thumb|Rubber tyred gantry crane loading a [[Intermodal container#Specifications|40 foot container]]]]
[[Image:Kuantan Port Container Yard with Rubber Tyre Gantry.JPG|thumb|right|[[Kuantan Port]] container yard with rubber-tyred gantry crane.]]
[[File:RTG crane by Konecranes SignalPAD.jpg|thumb|Rubber tyred gantry crane]]

A '''rubber tyred gantry crane''' (US: '''rubber tired gantry crane''')/ '''RTG''' ('''crane'''), or sometimes '''transtainer''', is a wheeled mobile [[gantry crane]] operated to ground or stack [[intermodal container]]s. Inbound containers are stored for future pickup by drayage trucks, and outbound are stored for future loading onto vessels. RTGs typically straddle multiple lanes, with one lane reserved for container transfers. <ref>{{Cite web|title=Rubber Tyred Gantry Crane {{!}} Amsak Cranes Private Limited|url=https://amsakcranes.com/product/rubber-tyre-cranes/|website=amsakcranes.com}}</ref>
Advantages:its mobility gives a rubber tyred gantry crane wide appliance

Being mobile, RTGs are often powered by [[diesel generator]] systems (gensets) of {{cvt|100 to 600|kW|hp|0}}. Due to the lack of an electrical grid to dump energy when containers are being lowered they often have large [[resistor]] packs to rapidly dissipate the energy of a lowering or decelerating container.<ref name=V>[https://www.calnetix.com/sites/default/files/VYCON_080421GantryCranePaper.pdf Fuel Saving Flywheel Technology for Rubber Tired Gantry Cranes in World Ports]</ref> Diesel-powered RTGs are notorious polluters at ports, as each burns up to {{convert|10|USgal/h|impgal/h L/h|lk=on}} of [[diesel fuel]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=US and Global Trade: LA, SSA Marine launch electrification effort to meet emission goals|url=https://www.joc.com/port-news/us-ports/port-long-beach/long-beach-ssa-marine-launch-electrification-effort-meet-emission-goals_20180405.html|website=www.joc.com|access-date=2020-05-26}}</ref>

There are also electric rubber tired gantry cranes.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kalmar Zero Emission RTG {{!}} Kalmarglobal|url=https://www.kalmarglobal.com/equipment-services/rtg-cranes/zero-emission/|website=www.kalmarglobal.com|access-date=2020-05-26}}</ref> The first electrified rubber-tyred gantry cranes (ERTG) in China was unveiled by the She Kou container terminal (SCT) in [[Shenzhen]] in Aug 2008. Rubber-tired gantry cranes are also being electrified at the [[Port of Long Beach]] to improve air quality, with funding from the [[California Energy Commission]].<ref name=":0" />

Aside from the intermodal industry, RTGs also are extensively used in industry. Applications include erecting large unbalanced structures, assembling large manufacturing components, positioning pipelines, and bridge construction.

Some RTGs use automation technology at ports to reduce human involvement in processing and handling cargo. Automation technology is used to optimize, track, or communicate container movements (e.g., automated gate systems), as well as automated cargo handling equipment to load, unload, and move containers. <ref>{{Cite web |last=Office |first=U. S. Government Accountability |title=Port Infrastructure: U.S. Ports Have Adopted Some Automation Technologies and Report Varied Effects {{!}} U.S. GAO |url=https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-24-106498 |access-date=2024-10-17 |website=www.gao.gov |language=en}}</ref>
